dimensions.assessment: Affects specific hydropower project licensees holding licenses issued before March 13, 2020, and the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission.
dimensions.evidence: on the request of a licensee of a covered project, the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission may... extend... the period during which the licensee is required to commence construction

dimensions.assessment: Provides significant schedule relief—up to six additional years of construction time split into consecutive periods—and allows expired licenses to be reinstated.
dimensions.evidence: extend in accordance with subsection (c) the period during which the licensee is required to commence construction of the covered project for not more than an additional 6 years

dimensions.assessment: No direct federal spending or revenue changes are stated.
Grants specific discretionary authority to FERC regarding construction deadlines and license reinstatements for a defined category of hydropower projects.
dimensions.evidence: authorizes the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) to extend construction deadlines for hydropower projects that were issued a license before March 13, 2020

dimensions.assessment: Temporary or project-specific relief lasting up to six additional years per qualifying project, structured in consecutive two-year periods.
dimensions.evidence: consist of not more than 3 consecutive 2-year periods

missing_information: Exact number of hydropower projects or licensees meeting the pre-March 13, 2020 criteria
Geographic locations or total megawatt capacity of the affected projects
importance_detail.rationale: This bill authorizes the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to extend construction deadlines by up to six years for specific hydropower project licensees whose licenses were issued before March 13, 2020, and allows certain expired licenses to be reinstated.
